description: AGM commentary — margin voice for the Franchise Book. One selected per era chapter + one per milestone flag. The AGM speaks like an old-school broadcaster: terse, cliched on purpose, occasionally poetic.

ascent: Football men will tell you an ascent is the rarest thing in this league. Winning is hard. Learning how to win is harder.
The arrow was pointing up for the first time in a long time. Everyone in the building could feel it, and most of them had stopped feeling anything at all.
This is the era a franchise decides to be serious. The wins were nice. The standards were better.
They call it the hardest record to beat in football — the jump from six wins to ten. This front office beat it.
peak: I saw every Sunday of this stretch, and I'll tell you what I told anyone who asked: this was the real thing.
Ceilings get a bad reputation. Most franchises never see theirs. This one hit it square.
January became a month this team expected to work in. That's the marker.
Peak eras are measured less by titles and more by the weight of every home game. This team carried that weight.
golden: Dynasties don't introduce themselves. They just stop leaving. That's what these years felt like.
Rings are one thing. A decade of rings is another language altogether.
You measure golden eras the way you measure earthquakes: by what they leave behind.
There are fifteen or so of these stretches in the entire history of the league. This was one of them.
valley: Nobody wants to coach through a valley. Somebody has to. That's the job.
I don't romanticize losing. Nobody in that locker room did either. But they kept the standards, and that's not nothing.
The scoreboard was ugly. The foundation wasn't. Those are two different conversations.
A valley is the front office telling the truth to itself, one Sunday at a time.
rebuild: Rebuilds are the bravest move in football. Admit it publicly, then actually do it. Almost nobody does both.
The record sheet says losses. The plan says assets. Those are different ledgers.
They traded today for tomorrow. That's the whole bet. Sometimes tomorrow arrives. Sometimes it doesn't.
You don't judge a rebuild by its middle. You judge it by what replaces it.
turbulent: I've watched this league for a long time and I cannot tell you what this era was. Neither could they.
Consistency is the hardest thing in football. This team did not have it, and the schedule did not care.
Some eras have a single voice. This one had six, all arguing.
When everyone's a different team every October, somebody is lying in August.
steady: Steady is underrated. It keeps the lights on. It keeps the fans coming back. It keeps the building professional.
Every franchise needs a stretch like this — competent, stable, unshowy, honest football.
You don't win a trophy for being a worthy opponent. But the league respects it, and I do too.
Nine wins most years. That's how you build the next era without burning this one.

byMilestoneFlag.three_peat_plus: Three rings in a single era is a monument. Everyone else is playing chess; this team was playing a different game.
byMilestoneFlag.multi_title: Two parades. Different rosters, same fingerprint. That's the mark of a real organization.
byMilestoneFlag.first_title: The first one is the hardest one. I've seen it break men who couldn't get there. This building earned it.
byMilestoneFlag.sustained_dominance: Win rates don't lie. This was not luck. This was a system that kept working.
byMilestoneFlag.deep_valley: The floor this team found is a floor I don't wish on any franchise. Credit to the people who didn't quit on the building.
byMilestoneFlag.dynasty_run: This is the era other franchises are going to study for twenty years. Every pick, every handshake, every handoff.
byMilestoneFlag.rollercoaster: Watch the schedule from this era in order and tell me what team it is. You can't. Neither can I.

byTrigger.championship: The chapter closed with a parade. Not every era gets that. Every fanbase wants it.
byTrigger.collapse: You don't close a chapter on a collapse unless the collapse was the whole chapter. In this case, it was.
byTrigger.era_gap: There's a missing year here — a silence the franchise chose not to fill. The chapter ends, the reasons remain private.
byTrigger.rebuild: The front office called it. That's the trigger. You can't sneak a rebuild past this league.
byTrigger.user_named: The ownership titled this era themselves. That tells you everything about how they remember it.
byTrigger.origin: Every franchise's book starts somewhere. This is where theirs does.
